"Unai taught me everything about football," Jackson told Sky Sports in 2025. And with Emery guiding him once more, it seems as if class is back in session.

articles.title: Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by Infantino
articles.summary: Infantino said in 2023 equality was Fifa’s target. Prize money could double but big gap will remain. Fifa is to fall short of gender equality with the prize money on offer at next year’s Women’s World Cup, despite making a record $15bn (£11.2bn) in revenue from this summer’s men’s tournament.
body: Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s “ambition” was to have “equality” for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.” There had, therefore, been widespread hope across the women’s game that 2027’s prize pot would match the men’s on at least a per-team basis.

There were 48 teams at the men’s event and 32 women’s teams will participate in Brazil next summer, so a women’s pot two-thirds the size of the men’s $655m would have been regarded as parity, but it is understood the women’s prize money will be about a third of the men’s.

That does mark a substantial increase. Some sources with knowledge of the extensive negotiations that have taken place in recent weeks are privately praising the rise, but one senior female source described the news as a “huge missed open goal” by Fifa. No decision is expected to be confirmed until December’s Fifa council meeting.

articles.title: Roster rifts, police raids and Son’s uncertain future leave South Korea at a crossroads
articles.summary: After a disaster World Cup, the team have continued to spiral, with tensions high between young and older players and the captain’s standing in question. Son Heung-min and Cristiano Ronaldo are iconic No 7s, Premier League legends and international record-breakers.
body: On 21 October, during a parliamentary committee meeting, politician Jeong Yeon-wook put a question to acting Korea Football Association (KFA) president Lee Yong-soo, that took a story out of the sports pages and into the national conversation. “It is said that recently, within the national team squad, players have been calling him not by his name but as ‘No 7’ or ‘that person’. Do you know who that is?” Lee then replied, “Are you referring to Son Heung-min?” Jeong went on: “So it appears to be true. … It has also been revealed that the national team’s leadership is causing discord and has broken down overall.” Lee declined to comment.

How has it come to this? Less than 18 months ago, Son was lifting the Europa League trophy as Tottenham Hotspur captain. That was his last act for the London club after a decade in the Premier League, during which he became a face of the world’s most popular domestic league and a huge star back home. Then came a move to Los Angeles FC in Major League Soccer, one the 34-year-old said was made partly to prepare for the 2026 World Cup.

articles.title: Dart stuns Badosa to make second career semi-final
articles.summary: Harriet Dart reaches the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career as she fights back from a set down to beat Paula Badosa in the Guangzhou Open.
body: Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career when she fought back from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa at the Guangzhou Open in China.
The 30-year-old triumphed 3-6 6-2 6-4 against Spain's Badosa - ranked 54 places above her - in two hours and 15 minutes at Nansha International Tennis Centre.
Dart's first appearance in the semi-finals of a tour event was in the Transylvania Open in Cluj-Napoca, where she lost in straight sets to Karolina Pliskova.
She will face either American Claire Liu or 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran in the last four on Saturday.

articles.title: Prospective Gateshead takeover close to collapse
articles.summary: The takeover of National League side Gateshead is close to collapsing due to third-party involvement, according to prospective owners Flacks Group.
body: In an open letter, external written by the American private investment group, initially set up by Manchester-born billionaire Michael Flacks, the deal is in serious jeopardy after it was informed another party had agreed to buy the club from the current owners last March.

Flacks Group claims Shoreline Limited attempted to purchase the club but filed court documentation four months later to confirm that its agreement was null and void, and so proceeded to enter negotiations with the current ownership.
Flacks Group's takeover looked to be close to being completed earlier this month, subject to approval by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).
In finding out about Shoreline Limited's involvement, Flacks Group now claims that Shoreline has refused to respond to its inquiry over Shoreline's alleged involvement with Gateshead.

articles.title: Duckett promises 'confidence' in Australia ODIs after dismal Ashes
articles.summary: Ben Duckett insists he will not carry any scars from a miserable Ashes into next month's white-ball trip to Australia after he ended the Pakistan tri-series with a flourish.
body: Duckett arrived in Australia last winter with a reputation as one of the world's best all-format batters, but he averaged 20.2 with a top-score of 42 in 10 innings as England were beaten 4-1.

To compound matters, a video circulated on social media appearing to show Duckett in an inebriated and confused state during England's controversial mid-tour break to the coastal resort town of Noosa.
However, Duckett has an impressive one-day record against Australia, with 470 runs in six matches at 78.33, including hundreds at Bristol in 2024 and Lahore in last year's Champions Trophy.
After recording two more centuries at the Gaddafi Stadium in the last week, Duckett will head to Australia for a three-match ODI series starting on November 13 in Perth in an optimistic mood.

articles.title: Afcon to return to two-year cycle after Caf U-turn
articles.summary: The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a review into December's decision to host it every four years instead.
body: The African Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a U-turn from the Confederation of African Football (Caf).
In December, Caf announced that the tournament would be held every four years instead, but that decision has been reversed after a review.

Under the new plans, the governing body was planning an African Nations League to replace Afcon as its biennial tournament, but acknowledged that it would take several years to generate the revenue required to become self-sufficient.

"The decision by the Executive Committee to reinstate the organisation of the Afcon every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 Caf Member Associations, as well as those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent," Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in a statement.

articles.title: Why keeping Isak fit and firing is key to Iraola's Liverpool revival
articles.summary: Liverpool's patience with Alexander Isak is starting to be rewarded, with the record-breaking £125m purchase finally resembling the most expensive striker in Premier League history.
body: Isak's neatly-taken goal in Liverpool's 2-0 win over an in-form Brighton at Anfield on Sunday means the Swede has now registered in three straight Premier League games for first time since January 2025, when he went on an eight-match scoring streak for Newcastle.

What was equally encouraging for head coach Andoni Iraola was the way Isak and fellow £100m-plus recruit Bradley Barcola, operating on the right-hand side of the front three on this occasion, linked up for his goal as the France forward broke clear before locating Isak where he is most effective - in the six-yard box, between the width of the posts.

This was always the vision of Richard Hughes and Michael Edwards, the men who brought Isak to the club last summer for that British-record fee, as well as Florian Wirtz for a similarly hefty outlay, as they looked to build on the previous season's title win by investing heavily in just one or two marquee signings, rather than follow Arsenal's approach and spread the finances out so as to build a bigger, more durable squad.

articles.title: The 11 'What If' Plays That Won The Brewers Their First-Ever World Series
articles.summary: Beyond the obvious home runs, big hits and run-scoring moments, don ‘t forget these plays — one from each of the Brewers’ 11 wins — that helped lead to them winning their first World Series title.
body: We remember the Jackson Chourio walk-off against Mason Miller, the back-to-back homers from Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell off Blake Snell, the multiple four-run deficits overcome and the eight-run, two-out onslaught at Tropicana Field, but what about the little plays that led to those Brewers wins?

The Milwaukee Brewers didn’t simply small-ball their way through their dominant postseason run, but their scrappiness and constant pressure did lead to them winning many of the plays that could have gone either way in each series.
The first sign that this October would belong to the Brewers came immediately. Ask manager Pat Murphy, and there might have been some divine intervention.

When their ace Jacob Misiorowski lasted only four innings, they still pulled out the 3-2 victory against the Padres thanks in part to their stadium. They led by a run with one on and one out in the ninth inning when San Diego first baseman Ty France launched a fastball deep to left field.
